Every episode? No, not every time. But... a few times, yeah. After those late-night eating spells, I've gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just get so scared that all that food is going to show on me, you know? Like I'll wake up the next morning and my pants won't zip.

It was a boat of a car, but it had those rear-facing seats in the very back, the "way-back" we called it. My brothers and I would fight over who got to sit back there and make faces at the cars behind us. It was one of those Italian ones with the shiny chrome and all the dials and pressure gauges. Looked like the dashboard of a vintage sports car. I saw it in the window of this kitchen supply store downtown. The store was next to this amazing little bakery that made the best almond croissants. I used to go there every Sunday morning. The owner, this French guy named Claude, he always had flour on his apron and he'd give me an extra croissant if I came in right before they closed. He moved back to Lyon a few years ago, though. Said the winters here were too brutal for his joints. I get that, actually. My left knee has been acting up every time it rains since I fell on the ice back in '98. I was carrying groceries and just went right down on the sidewalk. Smashed a whole dozen eggs. Had to go back to the store and buy more, and the cashier gave me this look like, \"Weren't you just in here?\" \n\nBut anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the guilt thing. The guy who runs the place has this massive collection of vintage typewriters in the back room. He showed me an Underwood from the 1920s that still works perfectly. It makes this incredibly satisfying *clack-clack-clack* sound when you hit the keys. I always wondered if he owned multiple pairs or just washed the same ones every night. \n\nBut anyway, no, I don't really feel like there's any big emotional stress or anything driving it.
